# Quickstart
Source: https://docs.globalstack.io/quickstart

From an API key to your first wallet in a few minutes.

This guide takes you from zero to a funded-ready USDC wallet: authenticate, create a customer, and create a wallet for them. Every call uses the base URL `https://api.globalstack.io`.

## Prerequisites

* A **GlobalStack account** — request access from the [dashboard](https://dashboard.globalstack.io).
* Your **secret API key**, issued during onboarding. Keep it server-side. See [Authentication](/api-reference/authentication).

## Steps

<Steps>
  <Step title="Verify your key">
    Make an authenticated call to a read-only endpoint to confirm your key works. Listing supported currencies needs no request body:

    ```bash theme={null}
    curl https://api.globalstack.io/v1/currencies \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_SECRET_KEY"
    ```

    A `200` with a `"status": true` envelope means you're authenticated. A `401` with `authentication_failed` means the key is missing or wrong.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Create a customer">
    Wallets belong to a customer. Create one with their type, name, email, and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 `country_code`:

    ```bash theme={null}
    curl https://api.globalstack.io/v1/customers \
      -X POST \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_SECRET_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "type": "individual",
        "name": "Ada Lovelace",
        "email": "ada@example.com",
        "country_code": "NG"
      }'
    ```

    The response returns the new customer's id (prefixed `cus_`). Save it for the next step.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Create a wallet">
    Create a USDC wallet for that customer. Only `currency` is required:

    ```bash theme={null}
    curl https://api.globalstack.io/v1/wallets \
      -X POST \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_SECRET_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "currency": "USDC",
        "customer_id": "cus_...",
        "label": "Ada — USDC"
      }'
    ```

    You now have a wallet (id prefixed `wal_`) ready to hold and move funds.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Next steps

<CardGroup>
  <Card title="Get a quote" icon="tag" href="/api-reference/quotes/create-an-onramp-quote">
    Lock an FX rate before you move money.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Run an onramp" icon="arrow-down-to-line" href="/api-reference/onramps/execute-an-onramp">
    Turn stablecoins into local currency, settled to a beneficiary.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Stay idempotent" icon="rotate" href="/api-reference/idempotency">
    Safely retry write requests without creating duplicates.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Handle errors" icon="triangle-exclamation" href="/errors">
    The response envelope and the error codes to branch on.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

<Tip>
  Pass an `Idempotency-Key` header on every `POST` so a retry never creates a second customer or wallet.
</Tip>


# Webhook events
Source: https://docs.globalstack.io/webhooks/events

Every event GlobalStack emits, when it fires, and the exact payload you receive.

Webhooks tell you when something happens on your integration — a deposit arrives, a conversion
settles, a verification is approved — without polling for it.

Every delivery uses the same envelope. The interesting part is `event_object`: it carries the **same
body as the matching REST resource**, plus a few fields that only make sense on an event. So if you
already handle `GET /v1/conversions/{id}`, you already know how to read a `conversion.success`
payload.

## Subscribe by category

You don't subscribe to individual events. You subscribe to **categories** — families of related
events — when you [create a webhook endpoint](/api-reference/openapi#tag/notification-webhooks/POST/v1/notifications/webhooks),
and receive every event in the family.

| Category     | Events you receive                                                                                                                           |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onramp`     | `onramp.awaiting_deposit`, `onramp.funds_received`, `onramp.processing`, `onramp.success`, `onramp.failed`, `onramp.returned`                |
| `offramp`    | `offramp.created`, `offramp.funds_received`, `offramp.processing`, `offramp.success`, `offramp.failed`, `offramp.returned`                   |
| `conversion` | `conversion.created`, `conversion.funds_received`, `conversion.processing`, `conversion.success`, `conversion.failed`, `conversion.returned` |
| `transfer`   | `transfer.processing`, `transfer.success`, `transfer.failed`                                                                                 |
| `deposit`    | `deposit.received`, `deposit.held`, `deposit.confirmed`, `deposit.failed`                                                                    |
| `kyc`        | `kyc.approved`, `kyc.rejected`                                                                                                               |

<Note>
  New endpoints are created **inactive**. Store the `signing_secret` from the create response — it is
  shown once — then activate the endpoint with `PATCH /v1/notifications/webhooks/{id}`
  `{ "active": true }`. Nothing is delivered until it is active.
</Note>

## The envelope

Every event, in every category, arrives in this shape:

```json theme={null}
{
  "event_id": "evt_1b8dbe64-1f4e-5a2c-9c31-6d9a51a0f0c2",
  "event_type": "conversion.success",
  "event_category": "conversion",
  "event_developer_id": "int_01HXYZABC1234567890ABCDEFG",
  "api_version": "v1",
  "event_created_at": "2026-09-30T09:12:44.000Z",
  "event_object_id": "con_01KPBH8MD6R7YDJ82T4D6M3V1T",
  "event_object_status": "success",
  "event_object_changes": { "status": ["processing", "success"] },
  "event_object": { }
}
```

| Field                  | What it is                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `event_id`             | Unique id for this event, `evt_` prefixed. Stable across retries — use it to deduplicate.                                                                                              |
| `event_type`           | The event, e.g. `conversion.success`. Branch on this.                                                                                                                                  |
| `event_category`       | The family the event belongs to.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `event_developer_id`   | Your integration's public id. Useful if one receiver serves several integrations.                                                                                                      |
| `api_version`          | Envelope version. `v1` today; a breaking change to the shape bumps it.                                                                                                                 |
| `event_created_at`     | When the event **happened** — not when it was delivered. A retry keeps the original time.                                                                                              |
| `event_object_id`      | The id of the resource the event is about (`con_…`, `txn_…`, `tfr_…`).                                                                                                                 |
| `event_object_status`  | The resource's status at the moment of the event.                                                                                                                                      |
| `event_object_changes` | `{ "status": [previous, new] }` on a real status change; `null` when nothing changed (a replay, or an event that doesn't move the status). `previous` is `null` on a first transition. |
| `event_object`         | The resource itself. Shapes below.                                                                                                                                                     |

Signature headers and how to verify them are covered in
[Verify webhook signatures](/webhooks/verify-signatures).

## When each event fires

### Onramps, offramps and conversions

These three run the same lifecycle, so they emit the same six events.

| Event                                    | Fires when                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onramp.awaiting_deposit`                | The onramp is created and waiting for the payer's deposit. Show them `deposit_instruction`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `offramp.created` / `conversion.created` | The resource is created and accepted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `*.funds_received`                       | Your funds arrived and were recognised. Work has not finished.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `*.processing`                           | The conversion or payout is in flight.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `*.success`                              | Done. The destination has been credited. **Terminal.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `*.failed`                               | Could not complete. Read [`failure_reason`](/api-reference/failure-reasons) — it distinguishes a quote nobody funded (`quote_expired`) from a genuine failure. **Terminal.**                                                                                                                                     |
| `*.returned`                             | Funds were sent back to their origin. Also carries [`failure_reason: returned`](/api-reference/failure-reasons) — the one reason set while `status` is not `"failed"`. **Terminal.** For an offramp that had already been debited, your wallet is credited back for the full source amount — see the note below. |

<Tip>
  `funds_received` and `processing` are separate events on purpose — `funds_received` is your cue
  that the money is in, which is usually what you tell a customer about. Don't treat either as
  final; wait for `success`, `failed` or `returned`.
</Tip>

<Note>
  **A returned offramp refunds your wallet automatically.** If the payout had already been funded
  from your balance when the provider sent the money back, we credit the full source amount back to
  the same wallet. The refund shows up in [`GET /v1/transactions`](/api-reference/openapi#tag/transactions)
  as a `deposit`-type transaction with `source_type` of `offramp_reversal`, linked to the original
  offramp as its parent. No `deposit.*` event is emitted for it — `offramp.returned` is the signal,
  and the offramp's `source_amount` is the amount returned.
</Note>

### Transfers

| Event                 | Fires when                                                       |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `transfer.processing` | The payout has been submitted.                                   |
| `transfer.success`    | The payout completed. **Terminal.**                              |
| `transfer.failed`     | The payout failed, was cancelled, or was reversed. **Terminal.** |

A cancelled or reversed transfer arrives as `transfer.failed` — `failure_reason` tells you which
(`cancelled`, `reversed`, or another code).

### Deposits

| Event               | Fires when                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `deposit.received`  | Funds detected but not yet final — a crypto deposit seen on-chain before confirmation, or a cross-currency deposit that has just been priced. On the cross-currency path `destination_amount` is `null` when the balance is under the corridor minimum; `metadata.conversion_pending_reason` says why. |
| `deposit.held`      | Credited but withheld pending review. `metadata.hold_reason` is `tier_limit`, `payin_frozen` or `payin_disabled`.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `deposit.confirmed` | Settled and spendable from the wallet balance. **Terminal.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `deposit.failed`    | The deposit could not be credited. **Terminal.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

Two paths are worth planning for:

* **A held deposit sends two events.** `deposit.held` first, then `deposit.confirmed` when the hold
  is released. Don't treat `held` as final, and don't expect it on every deposit.
* **A [cross-currency deposit](/api-reference/auto-conversion) never reaches a terminal
  `deposit.*` event.** It stays at `received`, and the `conversion.*` events carry the outcome.
  Waiting for `deposit.confirmed` on that path waits forever.
* **A cross-currency deposit may arrive with no converted amount and no `conversion.*` events at
  all.** Below the corridor minimum it is recorded, you are notified, and its funds wait for the
  next deposit to convert them together. Treat a `null` `destination_amount` as "not converted
  yet", and don't sum it across deposits — see
  [Minimum conversion amount](/api-reference/auto-conversion#minimum-conversion-amount).

### Verifications

| Event          | Fires when                                                                                                     |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kyc.approved` | The verification passed. `customer.tier` is the customer's **new** tier.                                       |
| `kyc.rejected` | The verification was declined. Read [`failure_reason`](/api-reference/failure-reasons#verification-kyc-codes). |

Only final outcomes are sent. Intermediate progress — a customer opening the link, submitting
documents, or being asked to resubmit — is visible on
`GET /v1/customers/{customerId}/verifications` and does not emit a webhook.

## Payloads

`event_object` is the REST resource body **plus** event-only fields. Two groups of extras:

| Extra field                                                        | On                                    | Why it's there                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `actual_source_amount`, `actual_destination_amount`, `actual_rate` | onramp, offramp, conversion           | What actually settled, versus the quoted `rate` and amounts. Reconcile against these.                                  |
| `terminal_at`                                                      | onramp, offramp, conversion, transfer | When the resource reached its terminal state. `null` before then.                                                      |
| `transaction_hash`                                                 | onramp (in practice)                  | The on-chain hash of the payout that delivered your crypto. **Present or absent — never `null`.** See below.           |
| `deposit_timestamp`                                                | deposit                               | When the deposit was observed (on-chain time or the payer's transfer time), which differs from the row's `created_at`. |
| `wallet`, `customer`, `credential`                                 | cross-currency deposits only          | Which wallet the money lands in, whose it is, and which credential was funded — no second API call.                    |

<Warning>
  Reconcile money against `actual_*`, not against `rate`/`destination_amount`. The quoted values are
  what you were promised; the `actual_*` values are what settled. They are `null` until the
  economics are known.
</Warning>

### Onramp

A completed NGN → USDC onramp. Same body as `GET /v1/onramps/{id}`, plus the four event fields.

```json theme={null}
{
  "event_id": "evt_4d5e0a27-7a63-51a1-8c0b-2f8d43f7d901",
  "event_type": "onramp.success",
  "event_category": "onramp",
  "event_developer_id": "int_01HXYZABC1234567890ABCDEFG",
  "api_version": "v1",
  "event_created_at": "2026-09-30T09:12:44.000Z",
  "event_object_id": "onr_01KPBH802PXQQXT8ASJGE0QX2K",
  "event_object_status": "success",
  "event_object_changes": { "status": ["processing", "success"] },
  "event_object": {
    "id": "onr_01KPBH802PXQQXT8ASJGE0QX2K",
    "reference": "INV-2026-001",
    "status": "success",
    "quote_id": "quo_01KPBK123456789ABCDEFG",
    "rate_source": "quoted",
    "customer": {
      "id": "cust_01HXYZABC1234567890ABCDEFG",
      "type": "individual",
      "name": "Alice Johnson",
      "email": "alice@example.com",
      "tier": "tier_2",
      "created_at": "2026-09-01T10:00:00.000Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-09-01T10:00:00.000Z"
    },
    "wallet": { "id": "wal_01HXYZABC1234567890ABCDEFG", "currency": "USDC", "label": "Treasury USDC" },
    "payment_instrument": null,
    "source_amount": "10000.00",
    "source_currency": "NGN",
    "destination_amount": "6.046600",
    "received_amount": "6.044100",
    "destination_currency": "USDC",
    "rate": "0.000605",
    "rate_locked_until": "2026-09-30T09:42:00.000Z",
    "deposit_instruction": {
      "version": 1,
      "type": "fiat",
      "accountName": "GLOBALSTACK / FX ENGINE",
      "accountNumber": "0123456789",
      "bankName": "Access Bank",
      "bankCode": "000014",
      "expiresAt": "2026-09-30T09:42:00.000Z",
      "depositReference": "GSVRYTZ496CM",
      "message": "Include the deposit_reference in the transfer narration/reference so funds are correctly allocated to this deposit."
    },
    "failure_reason": null,
    "failure_reason_message": null,
    "metadata": { "order_id": "ord_demo_001" },
    "created_at": "2026-09-30T09:10:03.000Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-09-30T09:12:44.000Z",
    "actual_source_amount": "10000.00",
    "actual_destination_amount": "6.044100",
    "actual_rate": "0.000604",
    "terminal_at": "2026-09-30T09:12:44.000Z",
    "transaction_hash": "0x9f2c4b7e1a3d5f6089bc2e4a7d1f3b5c8e0a2d4f6b8c1e3a5d7f9b0c2e4a6d80"
  }
}
```

<Note>
  **`transaction_hash` is present or absent, never `null`.** It is the on-chain hash of the payout
  that delivered your crypto, so it appears on `onramp.success` and effectively nowhere else: an
  offramp pays a bank account and has no on-chain leg, and a conversion between two of your own
  balances moves nothing on-chain. Some onramp rails also settle before a hash exists.

  Treat it as a convenience, not a guarantee, and **store it when you receive it**: this webhook is
  the only place it appears. `GET /v1/onramps/{id}` does not return it, and a hash that reaches us
  after the terminal event does not trigger a second webhook — an onramp delivers `onramp.success`
  exactly once. If you need a hash you did not capture, contact support.
</Note>

### Offramp

A failed USDC → NGN offramp. Note `failure_reason`, the `null` `actual_*` values (nothing settled),
and that `terminal_at` is set because `failed` is terminal.

```json theme={null}
{
  "event_id": "evt_8c1a0f93-4b77-5de0-9a24-7c5f1b3ea882",
  "event_type": "offramp.failed",
  "event_category": "offramp",
  "event_developer_id": "int_01HXYZABC1234567890ABCDEFG",
  "api_version": "v1",
  "event_created_at": "2026-09-30T11:04:19.000Z",
  "event_object_id": "ofr_01KPBH887CCT3A53EW3F8R0VQG",
  "event_object_status": "failed",
  "event_object_changes": { "status": ["processing", "failed"] },
  "event_object": {
    "id": "ofr_01KPBH887CCT3A53EW3F8R0VQG",
    "reference": "PAYOUT-4471",
    "status": "failed",
    "retry_on_failure": false,
    "quote_id": "quo_01KPBK123456789ABCDEFG",
    "rate_source": "quoted",
    "customer": {
      "id": "cust_01HXYZABC1234567890ABCDEFG",
      "type": "individual",
      "name": "Alice Johnson",
      "email": "alice@example.com",
      "tier": "tier_2",
      "created_at": "2026-09-01T10:00:00.000Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-09-01T10:00:00.000Z"
    },
    "wallet": { "id": "wal_01HXYZABC1234567890ABCDEFG", "currency": "USDC", "label": "Treasury USDC" },
    "beneficiary": {
      "id": "ben_01KPBAP7WTDKQKW5B3R31VPNX4",
      "customer_id": "cust_01HXYZABC1234567890ABCDEFG",
      "name": "Alice Bank Beneficiary",
      "label": "Alice's salary account",
      "type": "fiat",
      "currency": "NGN",
      "merchant_reference": "ref_01HXYZ4K5ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRS",
      "details": { "accountNumber": "0039415616", "bankCode": "000014" },
      "metadata": {},
      "status": "active",
      "created_at": "2026-09-01T10:05:00.000Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-09-01T10:05:00.000Z"
    },
    "narration": "Payment for Invoice INV-2026-001",
    "payment_instrument": {
      "id": "pay_01KPBH895W6PH3WY1D9KZH3M5D",
      "beneficiary_id": "ben_01KPBAP7WTDKQKW5B3R31VPNX4",
      "type": "bank_account",
      "country_code": "NG",
      "provider": { "id": "prov_01KPBAP7WTDKQKW5B3R31VPNX4", "name": "Access Bank", "code": "000014" },
      "account_name": "ALICE JOHNSON",
      "account_number": "0039415616"
    },
    "source_amount": "100.000000",
    "source_currency": "USDC",
    "destination_amount": "165000.00",
    "received_amount": null,
    "destination_currency": "NGN",
    "rate": "1650.000000",
    "rate_locked_until": "2026-09-30T11:34:00.000Z",
    "failure_reason": "temporarily_unavailable",
    "failure_reason_message": "This transaction could not be completed right now. Please try again later.",
    "metadata": {},
    "created_at": "2026-09-30T11:02:12.000Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-09-30T11:04:19.000Z",
    "actual_source_amount": null,
    "actual_destination_amount": null,
    "actual_rate": null,
    "terminal_at": "2026-09-30T11:04:19.000Z"
  }
}
```

<Note>
  `event_object_status` reports the deposit event (`received` / `held` / `confirmed` / `failed`),
  while `event_object.status` reports the underlying transaction status (`processing` / `received` /
  `success` / `failed`). They describe the same thing at different resolutions — branch on
  `event_type`.
</Note>

#### Cross-currency deposit

A deposit into a [cross-currency credential](/api-reference/auto-conversion) adds three blocks —
`wallet`, `customer` and `credential` — so you can see which credential was funded, including the
payer-facing bank details, without another call. `destination_amount` is the **quoted** value in the
wallet's currency.


A held cross-currency deposit arrives as `deposit.held` with `metadata.hold_reason` and a `null`
`destination_amount` — no rate is quoted while it is under review. On release you receive
`deposit.received` priced at the then-current rate.

#### Who sent a fiat deposit

When money lands in a fiat credential, `metadata` names the payer as far as the bank reported them.
The same keys appear on `GET /v1/transactions/{id}`, so a webhook and a later read agree.

| Key                     | What it is                                                           |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sender_account_name`   | The name on the sending account.                                     |
| `sender_bank_name`      | The sending bank.                                                    |
| `sender_account_number` | The **last 4 digits** of the account number — never the full number. |

Three rules to code against:

* **A key you do not see was not reported.** Keys are omitted, never blank, so check for presence
  rather than comparing against `""`. Banks report these inconsistently: you may get the name
  without the bank, or nothing at all.
* **`sender_account_number` is a last-4, always.** Use it to help a human recognise a payment, not
  as an account identifier.
* **On deposits into a Paystack NGN virtual account, the bank and account describe the virtual
  account the money landed in**, while the name is the payer's. That rail does not expose the
  payer's own bank details to us, and we would rather tell you that than guess.

Crypto deposits carry no sender keys — the on-chain `from_address` in `metadata` is the equivalent.

### Verification

`kyc.approved` carries the verified `profile`. Identity-document numbers are **masked to their last
four digits** — we never send the full number.

`tier_upgraded_from` appears only when the approval actually promoted the customer. Fields with no
value are omitted rather than sent as `null`.

## Delivery

<Steps>
  <Step title="Return 2xx quickly">
    Acknowledge with any `2xx` as soon as you have stored the event. Do the work afterwards — a slow
    handler looks like a failure and gets retried.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Expect at-least-once, not exactly-once">
    A delivery can arrive more than once. `event_id` is stable across every retry of the same event,
    so record the ids you have processed and ignore repeats.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Don't rely on order">
    Events are not guaranteed to arrive in lifecycle order. Use `event_object_status` and
    `event_object_changes` rather than assuming the previous event already landed, and ignore an
    event that would move a resource backwards from a terminal state.
  </Step>
</Steps>

A given resource emits a given event **at most once** — so two upstream changes that map to the same
event (a cancelled transfer and then a reversed one, both `transfer.failed`) reach you once, not
twice.

### Debugging a delivery

| You want to                    | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| See why deliveries are failing | [`GET /v1/notifications/webhooks/{id}/logs`](/api-reference/openapi#tag/notification-webhooks/GET/v1/notifications/webhooks/\{id}/logs) — attempt history with the HTTP status you returned, error, and latency |
| See what is queued             | [`GET /v1/notifications/webhooks/{id}/events`](/api-reference/openapi#tag/notification-webhooks/GET/v1/notifications/webhooks/\{id}/events) — pending events, oldest first, with the payload that will be sent  |
| Replay one you missed          | [`POST /v1/notifications/webhooks/{id}/send`](/api-reference/openapi#tag/notification-webhooks/POST/v1/notifications/webhooks/\{id}/send) with the event's `event_id` as `event_idempotency_key`                |

<Note>
  Replay only delivers to an **active** endpoint — an inactive one returns `409 invalid_status`.
  Activate it first, then resend.
</Note>


# Verify webhook signatures
Source: https://docs.globalstack.io/webhooks/verify-signatures

Confirm each webhook delivery came from GlobalStack and was not tampered with in transit.

Every webhook GlobalStack sends is signed. Verify the signature on each delivery before you act
on it — it proves the request came from GlobalStack and the body was not altered in transit.

Signatures follow the [Svix](https://docs.svix.com/receiving/verifying-payloads/how) standard, so
you can verify them with an official Svix library in one call, or implement the check yourself.

## What's on each delivery

Every request carries three headers:

| Header           | Example          | Meaning                                                               |
| ---------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `svix-id`        | `msg_2gT8sV...`  | Unique message id. Equals the body's `event_id` with a `msg_` prefix. |
| `svix-timestamp` | `1718960400`     | Unix seconds when the delivery was signed.                            |
| `svix-signature` | `v1,g0hM9SsE...` | Space-separated list of `v1,<base64-signature>` entries.              |

Your **signing secret** (prefixed `whsec_`) is shown in plaintext **once** — when you create a
webhook endpoint or rotate its secret. Store it securely; you cannot retrieve it again.

<Warning>
  Verify against the **raw** request body — the exact bytes you received. If you parse the JSON and
  re-serialize it before verifying, the bytes change and verification fails. Read the raw body first,
  verify, then parse.
</Warning>

## Verify with a Svix library (recommended)

The library handles the construction, the multi-signature format, timing-safe comparison, and
timestamp (replay) checks for you.

<CodeGroup>
  ```ts Node.js theme={null}
  import { Webhook } from "svix";

  const secret = process.env.WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET; // whsec_...

  // `rawBody` must be the raw request body string, not the parsed object.
  const wh = new Webhook(secret);
  const payload = wh.verify(rawBody, {
    "svix-id": req.headers["svix-id"],
    "svix-timestamp": req.headers["svix-timestamp"],
    "svix-signature": req.headers["svix-signature"],
  }); // throws on an invalid signature
  ```

  ```python Python theme={null}
  from svix.webhooks import Webhook, WebhookVerificationError

  secret = os.environ["WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET"]  # whsec_...

  wh = Webhook(secret)
  try:
      payload = wh.verify(raw_body, dict(request.headers))
  except WebhookVerificationError:
      return "", 400
  ```

  ```go Go theme={null}
  import svix "github.com/svix/svix-webhooks/go"

  wh, err := svix.NewWebhook(secret) // whsec_...
  if err != nil {
      // handle bad secret
  }
  if err := wh.Verify(rawBody, req.Header); err != nil {
      http.Error(w, "invalid signature", http.StatusBadRequest)
      return
  }
  ```

  ```ruby Ruby theme={null}
  require "svix"

  wh = Svix::Webhook.new(secret) # whsec_...
  begin
    payload = wh.verify(raw_body, headers)
  rescue Svix::WebhookVerificationError
    halt 400
  end
  ```

  ```php PHP theme={null}
  use Svix\Webhook;

  $wh = new Webhook($secret); // whsec_...
  try {
      $payload = $wh->verify($rawBody, $headers);
  } catch (\Svix\Exception\WebhookVerificationException $e) {
      http_response_code(400);
      exit;
  }
  ```

  ```java Java theme={null}
  import com.svix.Webhook;

  Webhook webhook = new Webhook(secret); // whsec_...
  webhook.verify(rawBody, headers); // throws WebhookVerificationException
  ```
</CodeGroup>

<Note>
  Svix maintains official verification libraries for these and more languages. Install with your
  package manager — `npm i svix`, `pip install svix`, `go get github.com/svix/svix-webhooks/go`,
  `gem install svix`, `composer require svix/svix`, or Maven/Gradle (`com.svix:svix`) — and see the
  [full list](https://github.com/svix/svix-webhooks).
</Note>

## Verify manually

If there's no Svix library for your stack, reproduce the signature yourself:

<Steps>
  <Step title="Build the signed content">
    Join the id, timestamp, and the **raw** body with dots:
    `signed_content = svix_id + "." + svix_timestamp + "." + raw_body`
  </Step>

  <Step title="Derive the key">
    Drop the `whsec_` prefix from your signing secret and base64-decode the remainder. Those bytes
    are your HMAC key.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Sign">
    Compute `base64(HMAC-SHA256(key, signed_content))`.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Compare">
    The `svix-signature` header is a space-separated list of `v1,<signature>` entries (an endpoint can
    have more than one valid secret during a rotation). Compare your value against each entry's
    signature — the part after `v1,` — using a constant-time comparison. Accept if any matches.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Check the timestamp">
    Reject deliveries whose `svix-timestamp` is more than a few minutes from your current time, to
    guard against replay.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<CodeGroup>
  ```js Node.js theme={null}
  const crypto = require("crypto");

  function verify(rawBody, headers, secret) {
    const id = headers["svix-id"];
    const ts = headers["svix-timestamp"];
    const sigHeader = headers["svix-signature"]; // "v1,aaa v1,bbb"

    if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(ts)) > 300) return false; // replay guard

    const signedContent = `${id}.${ts}.${rawBody}`;
    const key = Buffer.from(secret.replace(/^whsec_/, ""), "base64");
    const expected = crypto.createHmac("sha256", key).update(signedContent).digest("base64");

    return sigHeader.split(" ").some((part) => {
      const sig = part.split(",")[1];
      return (
        sig &&
        sig.length === expected.length &&
        crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(sig), Buffer.from(expected))
      );
    });
  }
  ```

  ```python Python theme={null}
  import base64, hashlib, hmac, time

  def verify(raw_body: str, headers, secret: str) -> bool:
      svix_id = headers["svix-id"]
      svix_ts = headers["svix-timestamp"]
      sig_header = headers["svix-signature"]  # "v1,aaa v1,bbb"

      if abs(time.time() - int(svix_ts)) > 300:  # replay guard
          return False

      signed_content = f"{svix_id}.{svix_ts}.{raw_body}"
      key = base64.b64decode(secret.removeprefix("whsec_"))
      expected = base64.b64encode(
          hmac.new(key, signed_content.encode(), hashlib.sha256).digest()
      ).decode()

      return any(
          hmac.compare_digest(part.split(",", 1)[1], expected)
          for part in sig_header.split()
          if "," in part
      )
  ```

  ```go Go theme={null}
  func verify(rawBody, id, ts, sigHeader, secret string) bool {
      n, err := strconv.ParseInt(ts, 10, 64)
      if err != nil || math.Abs(float64(time.Now().Unix()-n)) > 300 {
          return false // replay guard
      }

      signed := id + "." + ts + "." + rawBody
      key, _ := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(strings.TrimPrefix(secret, "whsec_"))
      mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, key)
      mac.Write([]byte(signed))
      expected := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))

      for _, part := range strings.Fields(sigHeader) {
          if sig := strings.SplitN(part, ",", 2); len(sig) == 2 &&
              hmac.Equal([]byte(sig[1]), []byte(expected)) {
              return true
          }
      }
      return false
  }
  ```
</CodeGroup>

## Deduplicating events

The body's `event_id` equals the `svix-id` without its `msg_` prefix. Use either to deduplicate —
a delivery may be retried, and the same `event_id` arrives more than once. Treat your handler as
idempotent: record processed `event_id`s and ignore repeats.
